$comment: REG-342 / FORM P4-T5 admission, written 2026-11-18 under the owner's choice of option A (a hash-pinned Java class binds to a FLOW, not to procedures[]). flows[].metadata carries one key today, untrustedExtensionEntrypoint, the same shape procedure.metadata and panel.metadata already had. It is the model-side opt-in the generator pairs with a manifest entry (kind flow): without it a manifest entry attached to any flow by name would let a file next to the model replace an ordinary flow. NET EFFECT: +1 slot now; retiring procedures[] (REG-342, still open) removes the whole procedure family, far more than this one slot.

declarative.why: a map whose only key is a relative path into the sibling untrusted-extension-manifest.json; no logic, no ordering

notLower.why: it names hash-pinned Java code that the generator compiles into the app after the bytecode/AST safety gate; no expression, function or step can reference code that is not part of the model, and a Property is resolved at runtime, not baked in at generation

twice.note: both apps bind RegistrarEntidadeTrustedProcedure and RegistrarProdutoTrustedProcedure through it (they were procedures[] entries before)

enforced.note: tests, not a booted probe: a flow naming an extension generates the pinned class and a registry entry under the flow name; a flow naming one with no manifest entry fails closed; a kind procedure entry does not satisfy a flow reference; the metadata survives parse and compile

taught.bundleLine: README extension table (docs/content/readme.yml): `metadata.untrustedExtensionEntrypoint` on a flow | your own Java class (the flow keeps a placeholder step), pinned by hash in the app's `untrusted-extension-manifest.json`, admitted through the same bytecode/AST safety gate as a mounted plugin. Deliberately NOT in the compact AI authoring bundle: an AI author never supplies extension code, a person does.
